subject: Follow-up: VPC / on‑prem & air‑gap constraints — next steps
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: VPC / on‑prem & air‑gap constraints — next steps

Hi Sarah / IT team,

Thanks again for taking the call today. Short recap from my side so we have a shared reference and clear next steps. Please flag anything I got wrong.

Summary of pain points & drivers (as described on the call):
- Regulatory requirement: certain customers require data to remain on-prem and disallow public internet egress for ML inference.
- Network constraints: final production nodes must sit in an air‑gapped subnet or behind a managed proxy; no direct outbound to 3rd‑party endpoints unless routed via jump/proxy.
- Key management: customer‑managed KMS/HSM is required for at‑rest encryption for PHI workloads.
- Ops expectations: predictable latency (90th pct < 150ms) for synchronous endpoints; bursty traffic for model retraining pipelines.
- Timeline: pilot planned for late July with potential GA in Q4 if pilot goes well.

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Private VPC with customer‑managed NAT/proxy + Redwood private control plane (preferred for quicker time to pilot).
2) On‑prem VM/GPU appliance (air‑gapped) with local control plane and periodic offline sync for metrics/usage.
3) Hybrid: customer VPC with strict egress rules + outbound tunnel to a dedicated Redwood endpoint in your region (requires approved firewall rules and proxy config).

Immediate asks / next steps I committed to:
- Send our standard network checklist and example firewall rules (attached SOW-draft includes checklist). [Action: Ben]
- Get existing SOC2 / security artifacts to attach for procurement. [Action: Marissa]
- Technical deep dive with your infra team (30–45m) to walk the network diagram and proxy requirements. Proposed window: week of 6/15. [Action: Ben to schedule]

What I need from you to progress:
- Network diagram with subnets and egress policies (attachment placeholder in this thread).
- Confirmation whether outbound connections are allowed to a single IP range or must be fully blocked.
- KMS/HSM vendor and integration constraints (no external KMS?).

Attachments I’m including: SOW-draft-v1.docx (proposal + network checklist). I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep dive — defaulting to 6/16 or 6/17 unless you prefer another day.

Thanks — will keep this high level until the infra deep dive.

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear summary. This matches our notes. Couple clarifications from infra/procurement perspective: 

1) Air‑gap / egress: For the regulated customers in scope, production inference nodes must not have direct internet egress. We allow outbound to our managed proxy only; that proxy performs TLS interception and logs. Any external vendor endpoints must be explicitly allowed via the proxy config and pinned to an IP range.

2) KMS: We run HashiCorp Vault backed by an HSM. We cannot allow third‑party KMS calls to leave the VPC; preferred pattern is Bring‑Your‑Own‑KMS with an on‑prem integration.

3) Data residency: Primary tenancy is US East for now; some customers will require physical hosting within specific states later, but that’s not blocking the pilot.

4) Network diagram: attaching the internal network diagram for the cluster we’d like to use for the pilot. You’ll see a separate management VLAN and an inference VLAN; the inference VLAN currently has no NAT gateway and must remain that way for compliance.

5) Procurement: procurement will need SOC2 Type II summary and a statement on log retention + data deletion. They will also ask for a draft MSA and SOW.

I attached the network diagram (cloudhealth_network_diagram.pdf). I can join the deep dive on 6/16 at 10:00am ET if that works. Procurement prefers to review the SOW before the meeting — if you can share an editable SOW (docx) that would speed things up.

Sarah
